images.title: A number system is a fixed sequence
images.purpose: Shows that counting maps each object to the next symbol of a standard sequence in a fixed order, and that the written symbols are numerals.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. A row of five dots above a row of five symbol tiles, each dot joined to one tile, a brace under the tiles naming them numerals, and an arrow beneath showing the fixed order.
images.exact_structure: Top row: exactly 5 teal (#0072B2) dots of equal size, evenly spaced. Middle row: exactly 5 square tiles with white fill and dark outline, directly under the dots, carrying the symbols I, II, III, IV, V from left to right. Exactly 5 thin grey (#6B7280) lines, each joining one dot to the tile under it. Directly under the tiles, one thin dark brace spanning all 5 tiles with the label numerals under its centre. Below that, one amber (#E69F00) arrow pointing right, as wide as the tile row, with the label fixed order under it. Exactly 5 dots, 5 tiles, 5 lines, 1 brace, 1 arrow. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A number system is a standard sequence in a fixed order; its written symbols are numerals.
images.description: Shows that counting maps each object to the next symbol of a standard sequence in a fixed order, and that the written symbols are numerals.
images.context: Concept compares sticks, letters and Roman symbols; this image shows the shared core: an ordered sequence.
images.teaching_notes: The Roman tiles reuse the symbol sequence the child has just met.

image_decisions.why: The definition of a number system is abstract; a picture of objects mapped to an ordered sequence grounds it.
